question: What is the principal layout difference between the pathway grade crossing and the sidewalk grade crossing in Figure 8E-1?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The principal layout difference is the right-of-way relationship to the roadway. In panel A, the pathway crosses the tracks within its own independent "Pathway right-of-way," separated from any roadway; in panel B, the sidewalk runs immediately alongside the roadway within the "Highway right-of-way," close enough that roadway grade crossing devices can influence sidewalk users. Both crossings show detectable warnings on each approach to the tracks. Standards (mandatory): - "Detectable warnings (see Chapter 3C) shall be used at pathway grade crossings where pedestrian travel is permitted and at sidewalk grade crossings and shall extend across the full width of the pathway or sidewalk." (This explains the detectable warning strips shown on both panels of the figure.) Support (informational): - A pathway "is frequently placed in its own right-of-way on an alignment that is independent of any roadway," and if built parallel to a roadway it is physically separated by open space or a barrier so that roadway grade crossing devices do not exert influence over or provide adequate warning to pathway users. - A sidewalk "runs parallel to a roadway within the highway right-of-way and is close enough to the edge of the roadway's traveled way" that roadway grade crossing devices can frequently exert an influence over or provide adequate warning to sidewalk users. - Pathways are typically used by both pedestrians and bicyclists, whereas sidewalks are typically used only by pedestrians. Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 8E-1 shows panel A with a stand-alone pathway crossing the tracks inside its own labeled "Pathway right-of-way," while panel B shows the sidewalk directly adjacent to a marked roadway, both contained within a single labeled "Highway right-of-way," with detectable warnings on both approaches in each panel. [Image 2] The full page confirms the figure and the accompanying Section 8E.01 Support text explaining the pathway/sidewalk distinction. [Image 4] shows Figure 8E-2, illustrating how a sidewalk crossing relates to roadway traffic control devices, consistent with the sidewalk being within the highway right-of-way. [Image 3] and [Image 5] show pedestrian gate provisions and figures (8E-8 through 8E-10) but do not bear directly on the layout difference in Figure 8E-1. Citations: - Section 8E.01 Support §4 (p.1035) - Section 8E.04 Standard §7 (p.1038) - Figure 8E-1 (p.1035) - Page 1076 - Page 1077
gold_answer: The pathway crossing is on a separate pathway alignment outside the roadway, whereas the sidewalk crossing is part of the highway corridor alongside the roadway and crosses the tracks with the roadway.
